questions.prompt: What do the Runway docs say a Recipe is?

options.text: A prebuilt workflow that wraps several generations in a single call
options.explanation: Right. You do not have to orchestrate the steps yourself.

options.text: A single generation with a longer prompt and more reference images
options.explanation: A recipe wraps several generations, not one.

options.text: A saved prompt that you reuse by hand each time you make a video
options.explanation: The primer calls recipes prebuilt workflows. They run several generations in one call.

questions.prompt: Why pin a recipe to a dated version on client work?

options.text: Only dated versions can be waited on until the task is done
options.explanation: Both kinds return a task. They follow the same contract.

options.text: The behavior stays the same, not the newest stable one
options.explanation: Right. The Runway docs say a dated version pins behavior and unsafe-latest tracks the newest.

options.text: A dated version is always free of charge for client work
options.explanation: Nothing in the docs ties a dated version to price.

questions.prompt: When you define the tools for a chain yourself, who runs each step?

options.text: Your application runs each tool call and sends the result back to the model.
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs say your application can continue the flow for as many tool calls as the task requires. The Claude docs say your code executes client tools and returns a tool_result.

options.text: The model runs each step itself, with no help from your code or the vendor.
options.explanation: The Gemini API docs say the model does not execute the function itself. The vendors describe a call and a result.

options.text: The vendor's server always runs every step, even for tools you define yourself.
options.explanation: That holds only for server or built-in tools. For tools you define, your application runs the call.
